---
title: Where Compose fits: one view, set as the content
version: 1
---

**Compose does not replace the activity; it lives inside one.** Before Compose, an Android screen
was a tree of `View` objects, each a class with its own state, usually described in an XML layout
and attached with `setContentView(R.layout.main)`. Compose keeps the activity and the window and
replaces the tree with **one** view, a `ComposeView`, inside which it draws everything itself.

`setContent { … }` in `MainActivity` is the line that does it. It creates a `ComposeView`, makes it
the activity's content, and gives it the lambda to draw. A test can look at what is there:

```kotlin
// app/src/test/java/com/example/planner/WindowTest.kt
package com.example.planner

import android.view.ViewGroup
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.v2.createAndroidComposeRule
import com.github.takahirom.roborazzi.captureRoboImage
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config
import org.robolectric.annotation.GraphicsMode

@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)
@Config(qualifiers = "w320dp-h200dp-xhdpi")
class WindowTest {
    @get:Rule
    val rule = createAndroidComposeRule<MainActivity>()

    @Test
    fun theContentIsOneComposeView() {
        val content = rule.activity.findViewById<ViewGroup>(android.R.id.content)
        println("views in the content: ${content.childCount}")
        println("the view: ${content.getChildAt(0).javaClass.name}")
        content.captureRoboImage("screenshots/welcome.png")
    }
}
```

`android.R.id.content` is the frame every activity's content goes into, whatever draws it. The
task is `recordRoborazziDebug` rather than `testDebugUnitTest` because Roborazzi writes a PNG only
when it is recording; lesson 21 shows the other two modes, which compare against one:

```
ana@vm:~/planner$ ./gradlew --console=plain recordRoborazziDebug --rerun --tests "*WindowTest" 2>&1 | grep -E "STANDARD_OUT|views in|the view|^BUILD"
WindowTest > theContentIsOneComposeView STANDARD_OUT
    views in the content: 1
    the view: androidx.compose.ui.platform.ComposeView
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 17s
```

One view, of class `ComposeView`. Everything the planner will ever show, every list and button of
the next twenty lessons, is drawn inside that one view by Compose, which keeps its own tree of what
it drew and does not ask the old `View` system for anything. `createAndroidComposeRule` launched
the real `MainActivity`, and the last line of the test saved the content frame as a picture:

```schooling-figure
{"image": "data:image/png;base64,", "alt": "The planner on a screen 320 dp wide: the sentence \"No courses yet. Add the first one.\" at the top left, and the rest of the window empty.", "caption": "What the window showed, saved by the test: one sentence in the corner of an otherwise empty screen."}
```

The sentence sits in the corner because nothing told it to go anywhere else; lesson 6 is about
telling it. `@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)` is what lets Robolectric draw real pixels, and `@Config` gives
the pretend screen a size: 320 by 200 density-independent pixels, at twice the density of the
original Android screens, so the PNG is 640 by 400.

## The other direction

The bridge works both ways, which is how large apps move to Compose one screen at a time. A
`ComposeView` can sit inside an old XML layout, among ordinary views, and an old view can sit inside
a composable through a composable called `AndroidView`. This course starts with Compose and never
needs either; you will meet them in any codebase older than about 2021.
